title: Proximal DVT: point-of-care compression ultrasound
summary: Answer the question every emergency clinician faces: is there a clot in the proximal leg veins? Learn the anatomy, the two-region compression scan, the mimics, and where the result fits in the NICE pathway.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates, from first scans to supervisors.
outcomes: Place point-of-care compression ultrasound within the NICE pathway for suspected DVT
Identify the deep veins of the groin and popliteal fossa and how they relate to the arteries
Perform a two-region compression scan and recognise a non-compressible vein
Recognise the common mimics and pitfalls, then document and act on the result safely
references: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158). 2020, updated 2023.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolism in adults (QS201). 2021.
Hercz D, et al. Ultrasound performed by emergency physicians for deep vein thrombosis: a systematic review. Western Journal of Emergency Medicine. 2024.
American College of Emergency Physicians. Ultrasound guidelines: emergency, point-of-care and clinical ultrasound guidelines in medicine. Annals of Emergency Medicine. 2023.
Royal College of Emergency Medicine. Point-of-care ultrasound appendix to the RCEM curriculum.
